spec.title: Corporate proxy with single sign-on on native Windows (PROP-068 #proxy) — vibe-managed px, PAC, the system trust store, no leftover px.exe

p.purpose: **Purpose.** The suite proves the route on Linux against local fixtures: a forwarding proxy, a fake px, a private test CA (`crates/vibe-net/tests/px_lifecycle.rs`, `crates/vibe-registry/tests/proxy_route.rs`, `proxy_git.rs`, `crates/vibe-cli/tests/cli_proxy_px.rs`, the `vibe dl` tests). No fixture can reach a real corporate proxy that demands Negotiate/NTLM single sign-on, a real PAC file, a TLS-inspecting corporate CA that exists only in the Windows system store, or `px.exe` running as a Windows console process in a job object. The owner checks those here, on the real network, before a release that ships the corporate-env campaign (`campaigns/corporate-env-2026-11/PLAN.md`).

p.placeholders: **Placeholders.** This document never names a real address. Below, `%PAC%` is *your PAC URL* (for example `https://pac.example.corp/proxy.pac`), `%UPSTREAM%` is your corporate proxy as `host:port` (for example `proxy.example.corp:8080`), and `%INTERNAL%` is an internal HTTPS host your PAC answers `DIRECT` for. Do not paste real addresses into a bug report; replace them with these names.

p.isolation-note: Every command runs in `cmd.exe` (PowerShell is commonly blocked on these machines). The test uses a separate settings home (`VIBE_SETTINGS`) and project directory, so the operator's own `~/.vibe` is untouched; the last step deletes them.

facts.PRE-HOST: Windows 10/11 x86_64, logged on to the corporate domain (single sign-on available), no direct internet route: `curl.exe -sS -m 10 https://github.com` times out or is refused.
facts.PRE-PX: A vibe distribution whose installation carries `tools\px\px.exe` (`cargo xtask dist px --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc --out-dir <dir>` stages it beside `vibe.exe`), or any px 0.11+ with `[proxy] px_path` pointing at it. Check `px.exe --pac=%PAC% --test=https://github.com` exits 0 — the same check px's own docs give.
facts.PRE-CA: The corporate TLS-inspection CA is in the Windows system store (`certmgr.msc` → Trusted Root Certification Authorities), as on every managed desktop. Its PEM export is available as `%TEMP%\corp-ca.pem` for step 6.
facts.PRE-TASKLIST: `tasklist /fi "imagename eq px.exe"` lists no px before the test (stop any px you run yourself, or note its PID and ignore it below).

section.title: Setup
section.fence: set VIBE_SETTINGS=%TEMP%\mt08-settings mkdir "%VIBE_SETTINGS%" set PAC=your PAC URL set UPSTREAM=proxy.example.corp:8080 (echo [proxy]& echo mode = "px"& echo pac = "%PAC%") > "%VIBE_SETTINGS%\config.toml" type "%VIBE_SETTINGS%\config.toml" vibe self apply --show

p.EXP-SETUP: **Expected.** `proxy mode: px (from user config)` and `proxy pac: … (url, from user config)`.

section.title: Steps

facts.STEP-1-TEST-PROXY: **First check: `vibe dl --test-proxy`.** It runs the whole chain once against the default target (`https://gmail.com`, redirects followed and shown).

section.fence: vibe dl --test-proxy echo exit %ERRORLEVEL% tasklist /fi "imagename eq px.exe"

p.EXP-1: **Expected.** The effective mode `px` and its origin, the PAC source (`url`, from user config) read successfully, px found and started, `px --test` passed, `CONNECT` answered 200, TLS verified with the issuer chain ending in the **corporate CA**, accepted by the **system** trust store, an HTTP status, timings; a short green summary; exit 0. `tasklist` lists no `px.exe` afterwards. On a failure the table names each failed step with cause and fix (a `407` means the request did not go through px / single sign-on).

section.fence: vibe dl https://github.com/genotrance/px/raw/refs/tags/v0.11.0/LICENSE.txt %TEMP%\mt08-license.txt vibe dl --headers https://github.com/ tasklist /fi "imagename eq px.exe"

p.EXP-2: **Expected.** The file is written with its byte count and SHA-256 (`573a63da…21fa9`); `--headers` prints the status line and the header table, never an `Authorization`, `Proxy-Authorization` or cookie value. No `px.exe` remains.

section.fence: vibe self doctor vibe self doctor --json --network https://github.com/

p.EXP-3: **Expected.** Lines `ok network trust` (the system roots counted), `ok network pac`, `ok network px`, `ok network px --test`, `ok network connect`, `ok network tls`; `--json` carries the same rows under `network`. No `px.exe` remains.

facts.STEP-4-INSTALL: **A real install from GitHub through px.** In an empty project directory.

section.fence: mkdir %TEMP%\mt08-project && cd /d %TEMP%\mt08-project vibe init --yes vibe add org.vibevm.world/wal vibe install vibe transfers --json tasklist /fi "imagename eq px.exe"

p.EXP-4: **Expected.** The install succeeds; `vibe transfers --json` shows the operation's transfers with `"proxy": "px"`; no `px.exe` remains after the command.

facts.STEP-5-CTRLC: **Ctrl-C.** Start a long download and press Ctrl-C while it runs (answer "stop" when asked); then repeat and close the console window instead.

section.fence: vibe dl https://github.com/genotrance/px/releases/download/v0.11.0/px-v0.11.0-windows-amd64.zip %TEMP%\mt08-big.zip tasklist /fi "imagename eq px.exe" dir %TEMP%\mt08-big.zip*

p.EXP-5: **Expected.** After the stop: no `px.exe` in `tasklist`, and no partial `mt08-big.zip` (or its temporary file). After closing the window: within seconds no `px.exe` either (the job object ends it).

facts.STEP-6-PAC-SOURCES: **The three PAC sources.** Repeat step 1 with each: a PAC file (download your PAC once with a browser to `%TEMP%\proxy.pac`), the system settings, and a one-shot override.

section.fence: set VIBEVM_PROXY_PAC=C:/Users/%USERNAME%/AppData/Local/Temp/proxy.pac vibe dl --test-proxy set VIBEVM_PROXY_PAC=system vibe dl --test-proxy set VIBEVM_PROXY_PAC= vibe dl --test-proxy --proxy pac=%PAC%

p.EXP-6: **Expected.** Each run passes and names the PAC source (`file`, `system`, `url`) and its origin (`VIBEVM_PROXY_PAC`, `VIBEVM_PROXY_PAC`, `command line`). With `system`, px reads the Windows Internet Options / WPAD; if the desktop has no auto-config there, the run fails with a cause, not a hang.

section.fence: (echo ca_file = "%TEMP:\=/%/corp-ca.pem") >> "%VIBE_SETTINGS%\config.toml" vibe dl --test-proxy set VIBEVM_PROXY_MODE=none vibe dl https://github.com/ %TEMP%\mt08-direct.html vibe dl --test-proxy --no-px --proxy http://%UPSTREAM% set VIBEVM_PROXY_MODE=

p.EXP-7: **Expected.** With `ca_file`, the TLS step still passes (the system store and the file together). With `VIBEVM_PROXY_MODE=none` the download goes direct and fails as a timeout or DNS error whose fix suggests configuring `[proxy]`, and no px is started. `--no-px` with the upstream proxy and no single sign-on fails with `407` and the fix "use mode = px".

section.title: Teardown
section.fence: cd /d %TEMP% rmdir /s /q "%VIBE_SETTINGS%" %TEMP%\mt08-project del %TEMP%\mt08-license.txt %TEMP%\mt08-direct.html set VIBE_SETTINGS= tasklist /fi "imagename eq px.exe"

p.pass-criteria: On a domain-joined desktop without a direct route, vibe reaches GitHub through a px it starts itself from your PAC URL, a PAC file or the system settings; TLS is verified against the corporate CA from the Windows system store (and `ca_file`); every step names its cause on failure; and no `px.exe` is left after any command, after Ctrl-C, or after closing the console.
